description.narrative: This project aims to reduce access to electricity has severely impacted all aspects of daily life in Syria, particularly in conflict-affected urban and peri-urban areas. This project aims to strengthen the resilience of communities by enhancing access to stable and reliable electricity which is critical for access to essential services and improving economic conditions. The project will focus on the installation of eight electrical trans-formers along with medium and low voltage distribution networks in three locations in Damascus and Rural Damascus governorates. These installations will restore electricity to critical community infrastructure including health centers, schools, water pumping stations, as well as workshops and residential areas, directly benefiting thousands of vulnerable people and supporting early recovery. In addition, the project includes the installation of two solar photovoltaic systems to ensure uninterrupted electricity supply for two key health centers: Sbeineh Health Center, and Daraya Health Center. These PV systems will provide sustainable, clean energy and improve access to essential health services in the face of frequent grid outages, to support the provision of medical services for the inhabitants in the targeted areas. In total, the Action will address the immediate needs and challenges of electricity supply for 432,000 residents in the targeted areas
